prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: board_01.kicad_pcb contains a 1.3 mm wide F.Cu track with NO net assigned: (segment (start 16.51 24.13) (end 16.51 21.59) (width 1.3) (layer 'F.Cu') (net '')). Its two endpoints are exactly U1 pad 7 [VCC_5V] and U1 pad 8 [GND] of the ATMEGA328P-PU, and it also lands on the GND via at (16.6, 21.52). KiCad 10.0.1 DRC on the delivered file reports 10 shorting_items errors ('Items shorting two nets (nets VCC_5V and )'), 1 clearance error (required 0.3000 mm, actual 0.2400 mm) and 2 solder_mask_bridge errors against U1 pads 7 and 8; my own geometric check puts the gap at 0.0000 mm. The same track exists in the product's own Board IR (board_ir.json, net ''), so it originates upstream of the .kicad_pcb writer, not in the writer.
expected: Copper of two different nets must never touch. A track that lands on U1.7 (VCC) and U1.8 (GND) must either carry a net that both pads share, or not exist. A board with 5 V shorted to ground across the MCU's own supply pins must not be released to a fab.
evidence: My own DRC run: C:/Users/KIIT/cursor-electronics/.claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_01/drc_mine.json (10 shorting_items, 1 clearance, 2 solder_mask_bridge); segment quoted above read from board_01.kicad_pcb; my geometric check: evidence_board_01/analysis_output.txt ('OVERLAP gap=0.0000 mm  pad U1.7 net=VCC_5V ... || track net= F.Cu w=1.30'); board_ir.json tracks[] carries the same track with net ''.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: GND is not a connected net. The Board IR declares no GND track at all; the only return path is a B.Cu zone '(net GND) (name plane GND) (fill yes ...)' whose polygon covers the whole board but which carries NO filled_polygon in the delivered file. My union-find over the emitted copper splits GND into 5 isolated groups: {U1.8 + via (16.6,21.52)}, {U1.22 + via (24.2,24.12)}, {Q1.1 + via (28.0,24.12)}, {U2.4 + via (10.2,21.72)}, {C1.2 + via (12.6,35.52)}. KiCad DRC on the delivered file reports 4 unconnected_items (U1.8, U1.22, Q1.1 and via (10.2,21.72) each isolated from a different GND via) and 5 via_dangling warnings. Plotting the way a fab would, 'kicad-cli pcb export gerbers' gives board_01-B_Cu.gbl of 3,824 bytes containing zero G36/G37 region statements - no pour at all; the same plot with --check-zones gives 79,834 bytes with one filled region. The ground plane therefore exists only if a person refills a zone by hand.
expected: The board that reaches the fab has one connected ground net, and the pour is present in the file that is shipped (or the net is routed in copper). The artifact must contain the plane, not the intent to plane.
evidence: evidence_board_01/drc_mine.json (4 unconnected_items, 5 via_dangling); evidence_board_01/analysis_output.txt (per-net copper groups, GND = 5 groups, 0 GND tracks, 'filled_polygon token present anywhere in file: False'); evidence_board_01/gerbers/board_01-B_Cu.gbl (3,824 B, 0 x G36) vs evidence_board_01/gerbers_refill/board_01-B_Cu.gbl (79,834 B, 1 x G36, same command with --check-zones).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The request says the board 'lights an LED on the same board'. The emitted board has no LED. board_ir.json lists 8 components (U1 ATMEGA328P-PU, U2 DHT22, K1 SRD-05VDC-SL-C, Q1 2N2222A, D1 1N4007, R1 CFR-25JB-52-10K, R2 CFR-25JB-52-1K, C1 K104K15X7RF53H5) and board_01.kicad_pcb contains 8 footprints; the string 'LED' occurs 0 times in either file, no LED net exists and no current-limiting resistor for one does (R1 is the DHT22 pull-up, R2 the 2N2222A base resistor). The board's own name in the IR is 'dht22_relay_monitor'. The omission is silent - no error, no warning, no refusal.
expected: A board that lights an LED carries the LED and its series resistor on a defined MCU pin, or the product says it cannot build that part of the request.
evidence: board_ir.json components[] (8 entries, no LED) and nets[] (VCC_5V, GND, DHT22_DATA, TRANSISTOR_BASE, RELAY_CTRL, RELAY_COIL_NEG - no LED net); board_01.kicad_pcb (8 footprint blocks, no LED); grep -c LED gives 0 on both files.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The request says 'a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable'. What the board carries is the bare 4-pin sensor soldered onto the PCB: footprint CircuitOS:DHT22 at (10.12, 25.44) with pads 1..4 on a 2.54 mm pitch, 6.84 mm from the decoupling cap. No footprint in the file is a connector - there is no header, terminal, edge pad or header row anywhere - so no remote sensor can be attached on a cable, and the 10 k pull-up R1 sits at the on-board sensor instead of at the far end of a run. The board cannot implement 'on a 2 metre cable' as drawn.
expected: A cabled sensor is brought in through a connector at the board edge, with the data pull-up and any series/ESD protection chosen for the cable; the sensor body is off-board.
evidence: board_ir.json U2 pads 1-4 at 2.54 mm pitch on the board and R1 (CFR-25JB-52-10K) between VCC_5V and DHT22_DATA; board_01.kicad_pcb footprint list (8 footprints: DIP-28, DHT22, RELAY-SRD, TO-92, DO-41, AXIAL, AXIAL, RADIAL-2 - no connector).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1 has no clock and no way to be programmed or reset. U1 pads 9 and 10 (XTAL1/PB6, XTAL2/PB7) and pad 1 (RESET/PC6) are on no net, and the parts list holds no 16 MHz crystal, no load capacitors, no ISP header and no reset switch. The Microchip ATmega328P DIP-28 pin table gives 9 = XTAL1/PB6, 10 = XTAL2/PB7, 1 = RESET/PC6; with no crystal fitted the part runs from its internal 8 MHz RC oscillator, half the 16 MHz an Arduino Uno is built and compiled for. So the board cannot take 16 MHz firmware and cannot be loaded without an external programmer.
expected: An Arduino Uno standing on its own board carries a 16 MHz crystal and load capacitors on pins 9/10, a reset network on pin 1, and a programming interface (ISP header or USB-UART bridge) so the firmware can be loaded.
evidence: board_ir.json U1 pads ('9',''), ('10',''), ('1','') and components[] (no crystal, no header, no reset); Microchip ATmega328P datasheet pin table, also in KiCad's public symbol MCU_Microchip_ATmega::ATmega328P-P (1 = ~RESET/PC6, 9 = XTAL1/PB6, 10 = XTAL2/PB7, 7 = VCC, 8 = GND, 20 = AVCC, 22 = GND).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board carries no silkscreen at all. board_01.kicad_pcb names the layer F.SilkS exactly once, in the layer table; there is not one graphic, text item or reference designator on it, and the exported board_01-F_Silkscreen.gto has an empty aperture list and no draw commands. Every reference designator sits on F.Fab, a documentation layer that is not a legend. Consequently nothing on the board marks pin 1 of the DIP-28 (U1), the DHT22's pin 1 (U2), the relay's pin 1 (K1), the 1N4007's cathode band (D1) or the flat side of the TO-92 (Q1). The footprints come from a library 'CircuitOS' that is not shipped, so there is no other place to get the markings. The D1 case is the sharp one: for an axial 1N4007 the band marks the cathode, the board puts the cathode on the VCC_5V pad, but nothing on the board or in the file says which pad takes the band. A C-B-E transistor (onsemi P2N2222A, BC547) fitted instead of the E-B-C 2N2222A, or a D1 band in the wrong pad, both give a board that silently does not work.
expected: A board that will be assembled carries reference designators and polarity/orientation marks on the silkscreen, so that a 1N4007 band, a TO-92 flat side, a DIP-28 pin 1 and a DHT22 notch are unambiguous to the assembler.
evidence: board_01.kicad_pcb: 'F.SilkS' occurs once (layer table), 0 graphics on that layer; evidence_board_01/gerbers/board_01-F_Silkscreen.gto (469 B, empty aperture list, no draws); drc_mine.json lib_footprint_issues x8 'The current configuration does not include the footprint library CircuitOS'; each footprint's Reference/Value property carries (layer F.Fab).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: There is no decoupling at the MCU. The board has one capacitor, C1 (100 nF, Vishay K104K15X7RF53H5), and it sits 6.84 mm from the DHT22's VCC pad U2.1 but 14.54 mm from U1's supply pads (pcb frame: U1.7 at (16.51,24.13), U1.20 at (24.13,19.05)). U1's two supply pins carry their return through a via into a plane that is not filled in the file (see F-0002), so the MCU has neither a local cap nor a local ground reference. The flyback diode D1 is also 9 mm from the coil pins it protects (K1.1/K1.2 at x = 29.29), lengthening the loop the diode has to catch.
expected: A 100 nF decoupling capacitor at the ATmega's supply pins within a few mm, and the flyback diode close to the relay coil it clamps.
evidence: board_ir.json pad coordinates (C1.1 at (7.58,10.12); U2.1 at (10.12,16.47); U1.7 at (16.51,21.59); U1.20 at (24.13,26.67); K1.1/K1.2 at (29.29,26.71)/(29.29,36.71); D1.1 at (27.9,17.74)) - distances computed from the emitted IR; components[] holds exactly one capacitor.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board does not obey its own net classes. board_ir.json declares 'power' (VCC_5V, GND, RELAY_COIL_NEG) with track_width 0.8 and 'default' (DHT22_DATA, RELAY_CTRL, TRANSISTOR_BASE) with 0.3, but the emitted copper uses 0.2 mm on 16 VCC_5V segments, 5 RELAY_COIL_NEG segments, 12 DHT22_DATA, 3 RELAY_CTRL and 3 TRANSISTOR_BASE segments - the 0.2 mm stubs sit between the pads and the wider tracks, so they are in the current path of the relay coil (K1.2 -> Q1.3) and of the 5 V feed to the coil (K1.1). At the coil current (SRD-05VDC-SL-C, 70 ohm coil, about 70 mA) a 0.2 mm track is not a thermal failure, so this is the board breaking its stated rule rather than a burn-out.
expected: The net classes the board declares: 0.8 mm on the power nets, 0.3 mm on the signal nets, including the pad stubs.
evidence: board_ir.json net_classes[]; width census over the emitted segments (evidence_board_01/ir_vs_pcb.py): VCC_5V w=0.20 n=16 / w=0.80 n=26; RELAY_COIL_NEG w=0.20 n=5 / w=0.80 n=9; DHT22_DATA w=0.20 n=12 / w=0.30 n=21; RELAY_CTRL w=0.20 n=3 / w=0.30 n=6; TRANSISTOR_BASE w=0.20 n=3 / w=0.30 n=9; one netless track w=1.30.
